2nd December 2023"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"The following is the OSCE made to answer questions around my patient who's case report is in the following link:\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/riddhibhalla25.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/25-year-old-female-with-fever.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/riddhibhalla25.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/25-year-old-female-with-fever.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EQuestion 1\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat is microRNA and how is it being used in the treatment of dengue\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMicroRNAs (miRNAs) are ~19–24 nt non-coding RNAs that post-transcriptionally regulate gene expression by binding to target messenger RNAs (mRNAs). miRNAs are expressed by all metazoans and plants, as well as by several DNA viruses, and function as regulators of cellular processes such as development, differentiation, growth, homeostasis, stress responses, apoptosis and immune activation\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3621958\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3621958\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Cellular miRNAs are post-transcriptional regulators that could play a role in direct regulation of viral genes. Host miRNA expressions could either promote or repress viral replications. Induction of some cellular miRNAs could help the virus to evade the host immune response by suppressing the IFN-α\/β signaling pathway while others could upregulate IFN-α\/β production and inhibit the viral infection.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/jbiomedsci.biomedcentral.com\/articles\/10.1186\/s12929-019-0614-x#:~:text=Induction%2520of%2520some%2520cellular%2520miRNAs,and%2520inhibit%2520the%2520viral%2520infection.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/jbiomedsci.biomedcentral.com\/articles\/10.1186\/s12929-019-0614-x#:~:text=Induction%20of%20some%20cellular%20miRNAs,and%20inhibit%20the%20viral%20infection.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe pathogenesis of severe\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Edengue has been attributed to\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; immunopathogenesis which\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eelicited an abrupt “cytokine storm”, leading to vascular\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eleakage, hypotension and shock. The complexity of\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDENV infection is due to immune responses that can ei-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ether be protective or pathogenic. Exposure to any of the\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Efour DENV serotypes during primary infection might ren-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eder life-long protection against the same serotype. In-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ecreased risk of severe dengue is highly associated with\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eheterologous secondary infection, which is a subsequent\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDENV infection with a different serotype. Aggravated clin-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eical manifestations of dengue disease from heterologous\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Esecondary infection might be attributed to cross-reactive\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ET cells or the “antibody-dependent enhancement”\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(ADE). The dominance of cross-reactivity of anti-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ebodies or T-cell responses towards the primary infecting\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDENV serotype over the secondary infecting serotype was\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eaddressed in the “original antigenic sin” concept of sec-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eondary DENV infections .The involvement of cross-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ereactive T cell responses observed in severe dengue mani-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Efestations infers the pathogenic role of T cells in DENV\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Einfection. The original antigenic sin proposed that\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ecross-reactive memory T cells from primary infection\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emight have a lower avidity against the secondary infecting\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eserotype, which in turn, could result in suboptimal TCR\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Etriggering and subsequent production of high levels of\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETNF-α that contributed to vascular permeability and\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eplasma leakage. Several studies demonstrated the role\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eof CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in the resolution of DENV in-\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Efection, whereby serotype-specific responses of the T cells\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ewere seen in primary infection of DENV in humans and proliferation of CD4+ T cells responding specifically the NS3 produced IFN-γ that lysed infected cells.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENevertheless, skewed T-cell responses during secondary heterologous infection might contribute to the severity of\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ethe immunopathogenesis of DHF and\/or DSS.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EOn miRNA as a treatment modality:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EmiRNA-based therapeutic modalities\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn general, there are two miRNA-based therapeutic modalities: miRNA antagonists and miRNA mimics. The former approach could be applied to inhibit miRNAs with\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eundesired functions such as miRNAs which are proviral.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA miRNA antagonist is usually introduced as a chemically modified miRNA which is known as anti-miR or antago-miR that could complementarily bind to the mature miRNA strand. To date, several chemical modifications\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehave been introduced to antimiRoligonucleotides with\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ethe aim of increasing their binding affinity, stability and\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ein vivo delivery. The most commonly used chemical mod-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eifications include locked nucleic acid (LNA), a bicyclic\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERNA analogue in which the ribose is locked in a C3’-endo\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Econformation, 2’ribose modifications such as 2-O-methyl\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(2-MO), 2-fluoro (2-F), 2-O-methoxyethyl (2-MOE) and\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ethe modification of phosphorothioate (PS) backbone\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAmong them, LNA was reported to be the one with the highest affinity towards complementary miRNAs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPharma A\/S and Hoffman-La Roche as the miRNA chemistry for the very first miRNA therapeutic and administered as antimiR oligonucleotide targeting miR-122 for the treatment of HCV infection\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EmiRNA mimics are synthetic RNA duplexes which mimic endogenous miRNAs. They are introduced to replenish or to further enhance the levels of miRNAs which are crucial to control disease progression. These miRNA mimics provided a promising proof-of-concept for miRNA replacement therapy. The tumor suppressor miR-34 mimic (MRX34) is by far the most clinically advanced therapeutic mimic\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/d-nb.info\/1208110829\/34\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/d-nb.info\/1208110829\/34\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EQuestion 2: what actually causes mortality in dengue? Is there any record of dengue patient dying of a hemorrhage?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBleeding, shock and raised SGOT and SGPT levels were identified as predictors of adverse outcomes and mortality in dengue fever.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETwenty fatalities with 80 controls were analyzed. Clinical parameters of postural dizziness (OR 3.2; 95% CI 1.1–8.9), bleeding (OR 31.9; 95% CI 6.08–167.34), presence of plasma leakage (OR 64.6; 95% CI 7.45–560.5), abdominal tenderness (OR 2.24; 95% CI 0.79–6.38), and signs of cardiorespiratory instability at admission increased the risk of dying from dengue. Altered consciousness was exclusively seen in 20% of cases. Laboratory parameters of elevated CRP (OR 1.652; 95% CI 1.28–2.14), AST, or ALT \u0026gt; 500 IU\/L (OR 52.5; 95% CI 12.52–220.1) and acute kidney injury (AKI) (OR 103.5; 95% CI 13.26–807.78) during hospital stay increased the odds of dying. Need for assisted ventilation and multiorgan dysfunction (MOD) were exclusively seen in the cases. Multivariate logistic regression revealed bleeding at admission, AKI, and elevated hepatic transaminase \u0026gt;500 IU\/L to be independent predictors for mortality.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7222550\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7222550\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/riddhibhalla25.blogspot.com\/feeds\/245427139545757496\/comments\/default","title":"Post year old female with Dengue fever"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"** This is an ongoing case. I am in the process of updating and editing this ELOG as and when required.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENote: This is an online E Log book recorded to discuss and comprehend our patient's de-identified health data shared, AFTER taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHere, in this series of blogs, we discuss our various patients' problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients' clinical problems, with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis E-log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and of course, your valuable inputs and feedbacks are most welcome through the comments box provided at the very end.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI have been given the following case to solve, in an attempt to understand the concept of \"Patient clinical analysis data\" to develop my own competence in reading and comprehending clinical data, including Clinical history, Clinical findings, Investigations and come up with the most compatible diagnosis and treatment plan tailored exclusively for the patient in question.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECASE SHEET\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChief complaint:\u0026nbsp; Patient presented with chief complaints of body pains since 9 days and fever since 6 days, headache since 6 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of presenting illness:\u0026nbsp; Patient was apparently asymptomatic 6 days ago when she developed generalized body painsand joint pains involving the knee,ankle and metacarpophalyngeal joints, sudden in onset, aggravated on onset of fever and releived on medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E6 days ago the patient developed fever which was sudden in onset and of high grade ranging between 101 to 104F as measured by the patient on seperate occasions. Continuous, with no diurnal variation, releived on medication.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAt the onset of fever patient also developed headache which was diffuse throbbing type not associated with aura, dizziness, tinitus aggravated on raise of temperature and releived on medication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUpon the set of fever the patient visited a local RMP who prescribed her a paracetamol for her fever and asked her to get tested for dengue.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient visited a diagnostic centre in Nakrekal and was reported to be NS 1 positive.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn receiving report patient came to our hospital to seek treatment for the same\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn day one of admission that is 3 days ago the patient developed vomiting. She vomited 6 times within a day. The vomitus contained digested food. It was not blood tinged. No aggravating or releiving factors\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient also complained 4 episodes of loose stools 3 days ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHess test positive on day of admission\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEj4h2Fa-EoK5H7nkakvyrwVW12CLyeKGOE6E30NAPJMIW6QKFUH2FQJpr7xaM-3k-N9xxMUJ1mUX5c1oy_6CN1lVDUoKaOVA_L1C0IxaFumffWHPAKrdGxQP63hhx2ZN76UBu-8iT5FNtNtNa4xKSHZKO8-NOKlGeszDCtUzDVXOsk1Bo65PK74gVOeY0dG\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEj4h2Fa-EoK5H7nkakvyrwVW12CLyeKGOE6E30NAPJMIW6QKFUH2FQJpr7xaM-3k-N9xxMUJ1mUX5c1oy_6CN1lVDUoKaOVA_L1C0IxaFumffWHPAKrdGxQP63hhx2ZN76UBu-8iT5FNtNtNa4xKSHZKO8-NOKlGeszDCtUzDVXOsk1Bo65PK74gVOeY0dG\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient had abdominal tenderness on day of admission.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt has also been noted that patient said she went to visit relatives a week ago where there were a lot of mosquitoes and she says she developed the illness ever since.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDAILY ROUTINE\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBefore the onset of illness patient used to wake up at 8AM and eat breakfast by 9 Am. She then did some household chores and are lunch by around 2:30. The patient has a 6 month old baby who she tends to most of the time. She has a glass of milk by 5 PM and dinner by 9 to sleep by 10 PM\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESince the onset of disease patient complained of excessive lethargy but still tends to the baby and breastfeeds her regularly.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of past illness:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; No similar complaints in the past.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot a known case of diabetes,htn, tb,asthma, epilepsy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDrug history:\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Patient started taking paracetamol and antibiotics 3 days ago at onset of fever\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo other treatment history\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPersonal history:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Appetite is reduced since onset of fever.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMixed diet\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENormal bowel and bladder movements\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo sleep disturbances\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo addictions and allergies.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFamily history:\u0026nbsp; No significant family history\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMenstrual history:\u0026nbsp; 30 day regular cycle with flow lasting for 6 days and usage of 2 pads per day. Bleeding is not associated with pain and clots\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EObstetric history: P1L1, spontaneously conceived, full term LSCS birth to a healthy baby girl weighing 2.5 kg with no complications.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEnvironmental risk factors:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient reports that many people in her neighborhood have gotten dengue in the past few weeks.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EShe says she lives close to open fields and the area is clean with regular garbage disposal.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient beleives she acquired the disease due to a visit to relatives house 1 week back where there were excessive number of mosquitoes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGeneral examination:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EConscious coherent and cooperative.
